formula: Short adj + -er + than · Long adj: more + adj + than
when_to_use: Compare two things: short adjectives take -er, longer adjectives take 'more', and both are followed by 'than'.
when_to_use_ar: للمقارنة بين شيئين: الصفات القصيرة تأخذ -er، والطويلة تأخذ more، والاتنين يتبعهم than.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic uses one comparative pattern (أكبر من) for all adjectives, so learners mix '-er' and 'more' (e.g. 'more bigger') and sometimes drop 'than'.

examples.en: This book is more interesting than that one.
Flying is more expensive than the train.

common_errors.wrong: Cairo is more big than Aswan.
This is more interesting that that.
common_errors.correct: This is more interesting than that.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: This film is ___ (interesting) than that one.
The city is ___ (crowded) than my village.

quick_rule: 1-2 syllables → -er. 3+ syllables → more. Always + than. Never both.
quick_rule_ar: مقطع أو اثنان → -er. ثلاثة أو أكثر → more. ودائمًا + than. ومتستخدمش الاتنين.
mnemonic: Short word → -ER. Long word → MORE. Never MORE + -ER.
connect_to_speaking: Compare two places you know: 'My city is bigger and busier, but the village is quieter and more beautiful.'
